standard_prerequisites.name: Irreducible and nondegenerate measures on the discrete cube
standard_prerequisites.reference: source 460-491 and 536-538, with the irreducibility counterexample discussed at 544
standard_prerequisites.statement: mu is irreducible if every coordinate xi_{i,x} can be flipped with positive probability while the others are held fixed; irreducibility implies det V_1 != 0, and the converse fails.
standard_prerequisites.use: Irreducibility is the hypothesis that makes the characteristic function decay exponentially; nondegeneracy alone does not suffice, as the parity example at 541 and 544 shows.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exponential characteristic-function bound
standard_prerequisites.reference: source 546-552 with its complete proof kept at 555-583
standard_prerequisites.statement: If mu is irreducible there is c = c(mu) > 0 with |psi(t)| <= exp(-c<t,t>) for all t in [-pi,pi]^K.
standard_prerequisites.use: Bounds the second term of the Fourier split on Q_{N,K} minus A_N in the main proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Gaussian covariance normalisation and lattice scaling
standard_prerequisites.statement: V_N = N V_1, B_N = sqrt(det V_N) = N^{K/2} sqrt(det V_1), and L_N = N^{-1/2} mu[|V_1^{-1/2} xi-bar|^3].
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the prefactor and the truncation radius 1/(4L_N) of the local estimate.

core_obligations: Set up phi_N, xi-bar, V_N = N V_1 and L_N, and state the supporting uniform comparison |phi_N(t) - exp(-<t,t>/2)| <= 16 L_N |t|^3 exp(-<t,t>/3) valid for |t| <= 1/(4L_N) (source 2199-2211).

Prove that comparison in both regimes: the exponential decay |phi_N(t)|^2 <= exp(-(2/3)<t,t>) for 1/(4L_N) >= |t| >= (1/2)L_N^{-1/3}, via the Taylor remainder R(x) = e^{ix} - (1 + ix - x^2/2) with |R(x)| <= min(|x|^2, |x|^3/6); and the region |t| < (1/2)L_N^{-1/3}, via the expansion of log phi with |log(1+z) - z| <= |z|^2/(2(1-|z|)) (2213-2286).

Rewrite mu^{otimes N}(S_N = M_N) by Fourier inversion and split the difference from the Gaussian integral into the three terms of (summation): over A_N = {|s| <= 1/(4L_N)}, over Q_{N,K} minus A_N, and over the complement of A_N (2289-2302).

Show each of the three terms is O(1/sqrt(N)) using the supporting comparison, the irreducibility bound and a Gaussian tail estimate, then divide by B_N = N^{K/2} sqrt(det V_1) to obtain the stated N^{-(K+1)/2} (2304-2325).

proof_roadmap.step: Prove the uniform Gaussian comparison for phi_N: first reach |phi_N(t)|^2 <= exp(-(2/3)<t,t>) in the intermediate regime from the third-order Taylor remainder, then handle |t| < (1/2)L_N^{-1/3} by expanding log phi and chaining the estimates for |log phi - (phi-1)| and |phi - 1 + <t,t>/(2N)|.
Write the point mass as a difference of two Fourier integrals and bound it by the three displayed terms.
Bound the three terms by C/sqrt(N) and conclude with the prefactor B_N = N^{K/2} sqrt(det V_1).

difficulty_reason: The claim is a lattice local CLT for mu^{otimes N} on {0,...,N}^K with error C/N^{(K+1)/2} that is uniform over the maximum in M_N, so the proof must compare an exact point mass with a Gaussian density rather than a distribution function. The complete proof at 2289-2325 splits the Fourier difference into three pieces - the Gaussian comparison on A_N = {|s| <= 1/(4L_N)}, the far region Q_{N,K} minus A_N killed by the exponential characteristic-function bound |psi(t)| <= exp(-c<t,t>) coming from irreducibility, and the Gaussian tail on the complement of A_N - each shown to be O(1/sqrt(N)) before the prefactor B_N^{-1} = N^{-K/2}(det V_1)^{-1/2}. The first piece is not free: it needs the uniform comparison |phi_N(t) - exp(-<t,t>/2)| <= 16 L_N|t|^3 exp(-<t,t>/3) for |t| <= 1/(4L_N), whose proof at 2213-2286 is a two-regime argument that restarts at |t| < (1/2)L_N^{-1/3} because the cubic Taylor remainder is not small there.

dedup.scope: Targeted neighbours only: the public index for the fixed AHL 7 (2024) 1245-1299 source (search terms local central limit, random transposition, recombination, Kac, chaos), the two same-source prepared cards, the 400 retired claims and the probability scouting notes for source 1065.

compared.actual_statement: source 375-389: particle-number-uniform modified logarithmic Sobolev / entropy-production bounds for strictly separating generalized random transpositions
compared.difference: That item is an entropy-production estimate for the particle dynamics; the new claim is a distributional approximation of a single sum S_N on a lattice with an explicit N^{-(K+1)/2} error. The public index contains no local-central-limit entry at all, and the proofs share no span.

That card's proof package (948-1870) uses the Wild expansion, marked trees, the linearised generator and Wasserstein monotonicity, and never the appendix 2198-2325. The new claim is a self-contained Fourier estimate for a product measure, with a different hypothesis (irreducibility) and a different conclusion (a lattice point-mass error).

That card compares two nonlinear solutions on the recombination state space (1100-1106); the new claim approximates the law of a sum of independent copies by a Gaussian density and involves no recombination dynamics.
Different paper: a regularity lemma for a nonlinear Markov chain limit, not a lattice local CLT with an explicit error rate.

editorial_notes: The counted statement is Proposition prop:LCLT of Section 2; its proof is given by the authors in the appendix under the heading at 2193, and the appendix's opening paragraph 2195 is outside the spans because it is a reading guide rather than part of the argument.

The two supporting items (the characteristic-function lemma at 546-552 and Lemma BerEs at 2198-2212) are carried with their complete proofs because the main proof invokes them at 2308 and 2315; no separate count is assigned to either.
The companion theorem 591-604 is carried only as the technique pointer cited at 2290; it is counted as its own card and no part of its proof is needed here.

The source line 2290 begins with a stray typewriter character before the words Set z_N; this is a native source slip and has been left exactly as in the fixed publisher file, with no mathematical change.
